attachments.document_title: Landlord's rent increase notice (with any covering letter)
attachments.label: A1
must_show: date from which the increase applies
whether the form approved by the canton is used (for a graduated-rent step, whether it is in writing: art. 269d para. 5)
any threat of termination in it or in the covering letter
for an index-linked increase: the old and new index values
if the landlord gave no notice at all, that absence is itself the finding (art. 269d para. 2 let. a)
attachments.text:
Feldegg Holdings Ltd
Emmen

NOTICE OF RENT INCREASE
Official form approved by the Canton of Lucerne

Tenant: Jack Turner
Property: 2-room flat, ground floor, Talstrasse 26, Emmen

Previous monthly rent: CHF 1010
New monthly rent: CHF 1125

Reason for the increase: adjustment of the rent to the rents customary in the locality and the neighbourhood for comparable flats.

If you consider the increase to be abusive, you may contest it before the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving this notice.

Emmen, 24 March 2026
Feldegg Holdings Ltd
David Marti

attachments.document_title: Proof of the date the notice was received
attachments.label: A2
must_show: how it was delivered (registered-mail tracking, envelope or acknowledgement)
attachments.text:
From: David Marti, Feldegg Holdings Ltd
To: Jack Turner
Date: 20 April 2026
Subject: Your question about our letter

Dear Mr Turner,

Thank you for your message. As you asked, I confirm for your records that our notice of rent increase for your flat at Talstrasse 26 reached you on 26 March 2026.

Kind regards,
David Marti
Feldegg Holdings Ltd

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

text:
Hello there,

The reason Feldegg Holdings gives for wanting more money from me is, in their words, that my rent is "below the level customary in Emmen". Full stop. Nothing about their costs going up, no word about mortgage rates or heating or maintenance, and they haven't renovated anything or added anything to the flat. I've lived at Talstrasse 26 since May 2024 and the kitchen is still the same tired one from the eighties.

It also isn't one of those agreements where the rent climbs in fixed steps every year. My lease has nothing like that, just the one monthly amount.

I'm sending you the e-mail in which Mr David Marti confirms the date the letter reached me, 26 March 2026.

So here is the situation: in that letter Feldegg tells me my rent will go up from CHF 1010 to CHF 1125 a month. That's more than CHF 1300 a year extra for a small two-room flat. I'm an apprentice electrician in my last year and my budget is already stretched. My girlfriend Kate Müller says I should challenge it, but I have no idea how that works or whether I've already missed my chance, since it's now May.

The increase notice itself is attached as well.

Thanks a lot for looking at this.

Jack Turner
